newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa reverses to end mixed on NY weakness.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa reverses to end mixed on NY weakness.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures reversed course again on Friday afternoon to end mixed, weighed by commercial selling in New York.
July closed down two stg at 1,016 stg per tonne while September lost four to 1,032. Total volume stood at 6,637 contracts, but traders said most of that was crossed.

July gapped higher at the open and was greeted by a flurry of short-covering and fresh longs after New York closed strongly on Thursday, traders said. But gains were limited by origin sales, particularly in back months, to keep July from touching its initial resistance level near 1,038. July's high was 1,032.

But pressure heated up when New York failed to follow-through on Thursday's strength and draw in fresh buying to fill an upside gap up to $1,501. When disappointment set in there, speculators were said to have dumped their holdings.
Commercial selling in New York also held back prices, traders said.
New York's weakness spread to London and sparked some speculative selling that pushed July down past Thursday's high to fill its opening gap, traders said.
Traders were generally not concerned over the sell-off because it locked cocoa back into its immediate, comfortable trading range between about 980 and 1,040.
They said the market could continue sideways for several more weeks before trying to break out again.
Despite choppy underlying futures prices, no options changed hands.
